Closest established methods are leakage-safe target statistics: [H2O](https://docs.h2o.ai/h2o/latest-stable/h2o-docs/data-science/algo-params/data_leakage_handling.html) supports leave-one-out and out-of-fold encoding; [scikit-learn](https://sklearn.org/stable/modules/preprocessing.html) uses cross-fitting to limit overfitting, especially for rare categories. Applied to transitions, exclusion should operate on entire users: removing one occurrence leaves other occurrences from that user contributing to its feature. User-level cross-fitting assigns all of a user’s examples to one fold and computes their transition features from other folds, following the isolation principle of [GroupKFold](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/cross_validation.html). Recompute smoothing priors and normalization statistics from the permitted users too; smoothing alone does not remove self-contribution.

An inexpensive diagnostic, derived from these principles: construct each user’s set E_u of distinct adjacent directed edges using training histories only; aggregate C(e)=sum_u 1[e∈E_u]. For a training example belonging to u, exact other-user support is C_−u(e)=C(e)−1[e∈E_u]. No model retraining needed. Compare ordinary coverage mean[ C(e)>0 ] with user-excluded coverage mean[ C_−u(e)>0 ] over actual training targets. Ordinary coverage is necessarily 100% when every queried adjacent target edge entered the graph; the drop measures examples supported solely by their own user. Report unique-edge, distinct-user-edge, and occurrence-weighted results separately: one user can repeat a singleton-support edge many times.

Also report support buckets (1, 2, 3–5, >5 users), singleton disappearance rate, and paired changes in smoothed lift after excluding each user’s contributions to numerator, denominator and prior. Macro-average by category and optionally user. These quantify independent support and sensitivity; they do not establish recommendation accuracy or temporal validity, and require no validation/test interactions.
